claim: Source and documentation review of trufflesecurity/trufflehog at commit 4b8eb0e1e1052263d28bbfde7b4d3cb64a354aab (license AGPL-3.0), read from README.md at that commit. Repository description: "Find, verify, and analyze leaked credentials". Reviewer summary of the upstream documentation: Go CLI secret scanner that detects 800+ credential types and, uniquely, performs live verification by calling the provider API each secret belongs to, confirming whether it is still active. Requirement part it addresses (secrets-credentials): Serves "detect accidental secret exposure before publication" — scans filesystems, git history, and CI/CD systems for leaked credentials before they reach a release.

documentation_excerpts.text: To learn more about TruffleHog and its features and capabilities, visit our product page.
Are you interested in continuously monitoring Git, Jira, Slack, Confluence, Microsoft Teams, Sharepoint (and more) for credentials? We have an enterprise product that can help! Learn more at .
verified: Credential confirmed as valid and active by API testing
unverified: Credential detected but not confirmed valid (may be invalid, expired, or verification disabled)
unknown: Verification attempted but failed due to errors, such as a network or API failure

limitations: Source and documentation review at the pinned commit only: not installed, executed, benchmarked or compared with any other component.

The description and excerpts are the upstream project's own words at that commit; the reviewer summary was written by a research agent and checked by an independent fit review. Both are upstream claims, not measured results.
